rules.title: California Civil Code section 1950.6 (application screening fees)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable time value, capped at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted since 1998). No fee may be charged when no unit is or will be available, and the landlord must give an itemized receipt, process applications in order or refund the fee, and return unused amounts.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually with CPI from January 1, 1998
rules.status_basis: Code section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords of residential rental property and their agents charging applicants screening fees.

precedence.text: This section is not intended to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
